patch_resolves_note: The staged patch and the authoritative fixed binary agree on the repair: the fixed `ps_read_doseps` checks that the initial `fread(doseps->id, 1, 4, FD_FILE)` returned 4 before the DOS EPS magic-byte predicate can advance to `doseps->id[1]`.

nodes.description: The vulnerable crash path reaches the second DOS EPS magic-byte comparison even though only 1 byte of `doseps->id` was read from the file.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `doseps_second_byte_compare.magic_bytes=4` and `doseps_second_byte_compare.read_count=1` on the crashing original case.

edges.description: The same `fread(doseps->id, 1, 4, FD_FILE)` result captured at the guard site remains the active read-count state when control advances to the second-byte compare.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `doseps_magic_guard.read_count == doseps_second_byte_compare.read_count == 1`; the adjacent `c5_padded_len4` witness records the same equality at value 4.

root_cause_criterion.description: Before evaluating the DOS EPS magic predicate, `fread(doseps->id, 1, 4, FD_FILE)` must report that all 4 magic-header bytes were read.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original reaches `doseps_magic_guard` with `read_count=1` and still executes the protected `doseps_second_byte_compare`, violating the missing `read == 4` obligation. The fixed original is guarded on the 1-byte PoC (`read_count=1`, protected compare absent), and the closest full-read witness `c5_padded_len4` makes the same fixed assertion genuine (`read_count=4`, protected compare executes cleanly).
